title: CNN segmentation revealed optic-chiasm differences associated with albinism
summary: A CNN trained on MRI from healthy controls was applied to assess chiasm morphology in participants with albinism. Mean overlap with manual masks was about 0.44 in nine participants with albinism and 0.75 in eight comparison participants, indicating that the normal-trained segmentation fit differed between groups. This small proof of concept is not a diagnostic validation or clinical workflow study.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network for optic-chiasm segmentation

evidence.tested: The segmentation model was evaluated against manual delineations in small retrospective cohorts; no independent or prospective clinical evaluation is reported.
evidence.unknown: No independent, prospective or clinical-impact evaluation is reported unless specified in the tested field.
evidence.ai_role: The learned segmentation of normal optic chiasms provided a quantitative comparison of fit to MRI anatomy in albinism and comparison participants.
